subject: EdgePay POC — latency-sensitive shortlist and next steps
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex@edgepay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: EdgePay POC — latency-sensitive shortlist and next steps

Alex — great demo today, thanks for the time. Quick recap + our recommended candidate slate for the live POC and suggested next steps.

TL;DR: For EdgePay’s 99th-p95 latency SLO (sub-200ms p95 on 1–2 token outputs, 250–300ms p95 on longer flows) and tight cost targets, we recommend prioritizing two engine classes: (A) low-latency quantized variants for short completions; (B) a mid-size high-quality engine for fallback/complex generative cases.

Recommended shortlist (first-pass):
- rwd-latency-q2 (quantized 4-bit, aggressive kernels) — best p95 latency, lowest token cost (est. $0.002/token), expected slight drop on long-form coherence.
- rwd-medium-ft (8-bit, optimized KV cache) — balanced latency & quality, est. $0.0035/token, better on multi-turn context.
- community/gptx-compact-v1 — strong quality for tricky prompts, higher cost/latency, keep as canary fallback for quality-sensitive flows.

Tradeoffs at a glance:
- Cost vs latency: q2 < medium-ft < gptx-compact.
- Quality: gptx-compact > medium-ft > q2 for long, open-ended generation.
- Operational risk: q2 requires a short warm-up/regeneration policy to avoid early hallucination regressions; medium-ft is the safest default.

Deliverables attached: benchmark summary (edgepay_benchmarks_20270614.pdf), prompt pack (edgepay_prompt_pack_v1.zip), quantization profile table (quant_profiles_table.csv). The Drive folder link has the prompt sets and the perf trace snippets.

Suggested next steps:
1) Run a 48–72h quick benchmark on a sample of your traffic (we can host or provide a self-run script).
2) We’ll ship a prompt/guardrail pack (attached) and a small eval scaffold for regression monitoring.
3) Align on canary criteria (latency p95, quality score by your QA team) and a rollout window.

Can you confirm: preferred mode for the benchmark (hosted via our API or self-run in your infra), and an initial target date for the bench?

Thanks — Markus
Markus Klein
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

On Mon, Jun 14, 2027 at 9:15 AM Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com> wrote:
> Alex — great demo today, thanks for the time. Quick recap + our recommended candidate slate...

Adding a few operational notes from the ops side:
- Canary plan: recommend starting with rwd-medium-ft at 20% traffic and rwd-latency-q2 at 5% (for short completions only). If p95 stays < 220ms and quality score delta < 2% (your QA rubric), expand q2 to 25% over 2–3 days.
- Regression guardrails: use the provided prompt pack plus the quality-check webhook. We'll wire a daily regression summary into the Slack channel.
- Edge deployment tip: for EdgePay’s regionally distributed traffic, enable prefix KV caching with a 5-minute TTL for common prompts — this reduces cold-start p95 by ~40ms in our tests.

Operational concerns to flag: quantized engines (q2) can show brittle behavior on long, multi-step prompts. For any flow where you need sustained multi-turn context (>1024 tokens), default to medium-ft. We'll include automated detection of multi-turn flows in the bench harness.

I also noted Alex’s ask about 99th percentile — attached benchmarks include p50/p95/p99 traces and tail-sample logs.

Ben — can you prepare a one-page cost sensitivity (q2 vs medium-ft at projected RPS ranges) and drop it into the Drive folder by EOD?

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Product Manager, Inference | Redwood Inference
From: Alex Morgan <alex@edgepay.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgePay POC — latency-sensitive shortlist and next steps

Thanks Markus — helpful summary. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we schedule the bench run: 
- Can you call out expected p99 and p95 numbers for rwd-latency-q2 and rwd-medium-ft for our typical payload (avg prompt length 18 tokens, response 6 tokens)? We need p95 < 200ms for the short responses in our payments flows.
- For the regression guardrail, what exactly is captured in the QA rubric? Is that something our QA team can run locally against examples?
- If we opt to self-run the benchmark in our AWS account, what artifacts / scripts do you need from us to get started quickly?

Also — your note about KV caching is interesting. Does that require any client-side change or a server-side config?

Appreciate the attachments; I’ll review the prompt pack. We should plan a 30-minute sync after you share the p99/p95 expected numbers so we can lock dates.

—Alex
Alex Morgan
Platform Engineer | EdgePay
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex@edgepay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgePay POC — latency-sensitive shortlist and next steps

On Tue, Jun 15, 2027 at 8:10 AM Alex Morgan <alex@edgepay.com> wrote:
> Thanks Markus — helpful summary. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we schedule the bench run: 

Alex — quick answers and a proposed immediate plan: 
- Expected tail numbers (your profile: avg prompt 18 / response 6, US-west region, single-request concurrency):
  - rwd-latency-q2: p50 ~ 32ms, p95 ~ 160ms, p99 ~ 280ms (note: p99 can spike on cold-KV misses).
  - rwd-medium-ft: p50 ~ 45ms, p95 ~ 210ms, p99 ~ 360ms.
  These are from the attached bench traces (edgepay_benchmarks_20270614.pdf) measured on the same GPU class we propose for the POC.

- QA rubric: the scaffold includes 1) toxicity/safety check, 2) functional correctness checklist (binary pass/fail per prompt), 3) human-judged fluency/accuracy score (0–5). Yes — your QA team can run it locally; the prompt pack includes an eval harness (run_eval.sh) and a small instructions.md.

- Self-run artifacts we need from you: a representative sample of 2k prompts (anonymized), expected RPS profile (peak and sustained), and an IAM role if you want us to push temporary CloudWatch traces into your account. If you’d rather we host the bench, we’ll need a test API key and a simple firewall allowlist of your IPs.

- KV caching: server-side config; no client code changes required other than sending consistent prompt prefixes. We’ll provide a short guide in the Drive folder.

Next steps I propose:
1) You share the sample prompt file + RPS profile by EOD Wed (2027-06-16).
2) We run a 48-hour hosted bench (or provide the self-run artifacts) and surface p50/p95/p99 plus QA-rubric deltas.
3) 30-minute sync on Thu (2027-06-17) to review and pick initial canary percentages.

I attached the three deliverables again for convenience: edgepay_benchmarks_20270614.pdf (bench traces), edgepay_prompt_pack_v1.zip (prompts + eval harness), quant_profiles_table.csv (quant sensitivity table).

If that timeline works I’ll drop a calendar invite.

Thanks — Markus
Markus Klein
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
